newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Tyumentelekom sees strong 97 dividend rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian Tyumentelekom sees strong 97 dividend rise.

text.p: Russian regional telecom Tyumentelekom said on Thursday that it expected 1997 dividends to be significantly higher on 1996 due to changes in tax laws.
A company statement said that 1997 net profit and line capacity would rise and that first quarter results also showed profit and sales growth.

The statement estimated 1997 net profit, calculated on a Russian accruals basis, would rise to about 60.1 billion roubles, after 23.9 billion in 1996, in part due to doubling acceleration of fixed asset depreciation.
It said first quarter net profit, calculated on a Russian accruals basis, was $3.6 million (17.9 billion roubles), up 44 percent on a year ago.
Pretax profit in the same period compared to a year ago rose 13.5 percent to $3.5 million (19.9 billion roubles) and sales were up five percent to $14.2 million (80.5 billion roubles).
Sales calculated on a cash basis were 75.5 billion roubles and five percent of revenue was received in goods.
Previous law had allowed the Siberian-based provider to accumulate reserves from operating income towards capital expansion, which decreased tax burdens and dividend payout requirements.

"The accumulation of such reserves no longer gives any tax relief and so such dividends will be calculated on the basis of profit after tax without any decrease due to such reserves," a company statement said.
"Management believes this should result in a significant increase in dividends enjoyed by shareholders."
Dividends for 1996 were 44 roubles for ordinary shares and 266 roubles for privileged shares.
Company management expected the Tyumen regional administration to approve a 25 percent hike in residential tariffs in the second quarter of this year.
New signed agreements with Western vendors would boost line capacity to 238,600 lines by year-end, a 41,700 line increase.
Tyumentelekom's board has voted to issue level one American Depositary Receipts to trade on foreign exchanges but has not announced a timetable.
Tyumentelekom shares trade on the RTS-2 system for less liquid shares and were quoted at $2.95/$3.30 at the close on Wednesday. On April 2 they were quoted at $3.00/$3.90
